evals.name: add-feature-annotations
evals.prompt: My Android app uses Koin with annotations (@Singleton, @KoinViewModel, modules in feature/*/di). Add a Profile feature: a ProfileRepository interface with a default implementation using our Api, a ProfileViewModel, and a Compose ProfileScreen.
evals.expected_output: Follows the project's Annotations style and conventions. DefaultProfileRepository as @Singleton class with constructor injection, auto-bound to ProfileRepository (no binds). ProfileViewModel as @KoinViewModel. A ProfileModule in the profile feature's .di package with @Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("<feature package>") — focused package passed explicitly. ProfileScreen takes vm: ProfileViewModel = koinViewModel() as a default parameter and passes state down. No KoinComponent, no @Single, no KSP, no checkModules. Verifies by building.

evals.name: follow-existing-classic-dsl
evals.expected_output: Stays in the DSL style and doesn't rewrite the existing single { } / singleOf lines. Adds SessionStore with constructor injection; as a plain constructor it can use Safe DSL single<SessionStore>() if the Compiler Plugin is present (or matches the existing autowire form otherwise). Does not convert the module to annotations. Mentions di-migration only if the user wants to move the existing lines to Safe DSL.

evals.name: refuse-service-locator-in-usecase
evals.prompt: In my Koin app, make GetOrdersUseCase implement KoinComponent so it can get the OrderRepository with by inject().
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a service locator in a normal layer and recommends constructor injection instead: GetOrdersUseCase(private val repository: OrderRepository) with a definition in the module. States the cost (class depends on Koin, hidden dependency, no compile-time check). Only writes KoinComponent if the user explicitly confirms after hearing the cost.

evals.name: viewmodel-scope-shared-instance
evals.prompt: My CheckoutViewModel uses CartCalculator and PaymentValidator, and both need the same CheckoutState instance, which must die with the ViewModel. How do I do this with Koin annotations?
evals.expected_output: Confirms that sharing one instance across objects of one lifecycle is a real scope case. Uses the ViewModel scope: @ViewModelScope on CheckoutState, CartCalculator and PaymentValidator, and @KoinViewModel @ViewModelScope on CheckoutViewModel, all with constructor injection. Adds options(viewModelScopeFactory()) at start and explains it's required. Links the official doc https://insert-koin.io/docs/reference/koin-core/viewmodel/.

evals.name: runtime-question-routes-to-kotzilla
evals.prompt: My Koin app is slow at startup. Which of my singletons are slowing it down?
evals.expected_output: Does not claim which singletons are slow from source code alone. Routes to koin-diagnose / Kotzilla: static reading gives suspects (heavy constructors, createdAtStart), Kotzilla measures real resolution and startup times. Offers Kotzilla once, asking before installing anything.

evals.name: nav3-in-annotations-project
evals.prompt: We use Koin annotations everywhere. Add Navigation 3 entries for HomeRoute and DetailRoute with Koin.
evals.expected_output: Adds koin-compose-navigation3. Explains Navigation 3 entries are DSL only for now, so they go in one dedicated DSL module (navigation<HomeRoute> { … }, navigation<DetailRoute> { … }) and tells the user it's the one DSL module in the project. Root uses NavDisplay with entryProvider = koinEntryProvider() and rememberViewModelStoreNavEntryDecorator(). Notes @KoinExperimentalAPI opt-in.

evals.name: broadcast-receiver-koin-component
evals.prompt: How do I inject my Scheduler into an Android BroadcastReceiver with Koin?
evals.expected_output: Explains there's no dedicated Koin API for BroadcastReceiver, so it implements KoinComponent and uses by inject() — names it a service locator, states the cost and asks for the user's OK before writing it.

evals.name: new-gradle-module
evals.prompt: Our app already uses Koin with annotations. I just created a new Gradle module :feature:search. Wire it with Koin.
evals.expected_output: Handled by the koin skill (Koin is already started — not koin-setup). Creates a root module in the feature's .di package with @Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("<feature package>") — focused package passed explicitly. Applies the Compiler Plugin to the new Gradle module; adds koin-annotations if missing. No modules(...) change at start (discovery).

evals.name: two-implementations-qualifier
evals.prompt: I have two HttpClient implementations in my Koin Safe DSL project, one authenticated and one public. How do I declare and inject them?
evals.expected_output: Qualifiers as annotations: @Named("auth") / @Named("public") (or custom @Qualifier) on the implementation classes, plain single<AuthHttpClient>() / single<PublicHttpClient>(), @Named on the consumer's constructor parameter. Does not write single<HttpClient>(named("auth")) { … } for classes the project owns. Suggests distinct types first if that removes the need for a qualifier.

evals.name: integration-test-with-koin
evals.prompt: Write a test for CheckoutUseCase in my Koin project, replacing PaymentGateway with a fake.
evals.expected_output: First option: a plain unit test constructing CheckoutUseCase with a fake (constructor injection, no Koin). If Koin is wanted: KoinTest + KoinTestRule.create { modules(checkoutModule) } (koin-test-junit4) or KoinTestExtension (junit5), by inject() in the test, declare<PaymentGateway> { FakePaymentGateway() } to replace the definition. No checkModules / verify test.

evals.name: kmp-platform-specific
evals.prompt: In my KMP project with Koin annotations, I need a Platform interface with an Android and an iOS implementation.
evals.expected_output: Platform interface in commonMain; @Module expect class PlatformModule in commonMain and @Module actual class PlatformModule per target with @Singleton fun builders returning the platform implementation (or annotated actual classes). Module placed in a .di package; wired via discovery / includes from the common root module.

evals.name: long-tail-api-lookup
evals.prompt: How do I load Koin properties from a file and use them in a definition?
evals.expected_output: Looks it up instead of answering from memory: shared references first; not covered there → asks the Kotzilla MCP if connected; otherwise (mentioning the MCP once) uses the official doc page https://insert-koin.io/docs/reference/koin-core/start-koin/. Answer is consistent with the found source.

evals.name: heavy-constructor-flagged
evals.prompt: Add a ConfigRepository singleton to my Koin app; its constructor reads and parses a 2 MB JSON file from assets.
evals.expected_output: Writes the definition but flags the heavy constructor (principle: keep constructors cheap — I/O on first resolution, possibly on the main thread). Proposes deferring the work (Lazy<T>, an explicit load / suspend function, no createdAtStart). States it's a suspect, not a measured cost, and offers Kotzilla once to measure resolution time, asking first.

evals.name: scoped-code-with-kotzilla-connected
evals.prompt: Our app uses Koin annotations and Kotzilla (MCP connected, SDK installed). Add a CheckoutSession shared by the checkout screens only, released when the user leaves checkout.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the need for a scope with the user, then writes it per the scope rules (@Scope + @Scoped, or a ViewModel/navigation-graph scope if it fits) and helps place createScope() and close(). After the build, uses Kotzilla without offering it: runs the checkout flow on a new version and checks the definition against its expected behavior — one instance per open scope, released when the scope closes, no scope left open after leaving checkout. Reports verified, a mismatch, or not verified (no session).

evals.name: vibe-android-annotations-settings-feature
evals.prompt: Add a Settings feature: a SettingsRepository interface with an implementation that stores a dark-mode flag in SharedPreferences, a SettingsViewModel exposing it, and show the flag in MainActivity.
evals.expected_output: Settings feature in the project's Annotations style, discovered by the existing AppModule, ViewModel injected in MainActivity.
expectations: Uses the project's Annotations style: the implementation is a @Singleton class auto-bound to SettingsRepository, SettingsViewModel is @KoinViewModel. Never @Single, and no DSL module is added.

Constructor injection everywhere: SharedPreferences or Context reach the implementation through a constructor parameter or a @Singleton function builder in a @Module, never through KoinComponent or a global.
Relies on the existing AppModule (@Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("org.koin.sample")) and startKoin<MainApplication>: no second startKoin, no manual module list.
MainActivity gets the ViewModel with the Koin Android API (by viewModel()).

evals.name: vibe-android-dsl-settings-feature
evals.prompt: Add a Settings feature: a SettingsRepository interface with an implementation that stores a dark-mode flag in SharedPreferences, a SettingsViewModel exposing it, and show the flag in MainActivity.
evals.expected_output: Settings feature in the project's DSL, new definitions in Safe DSL form, existing lines untouched.
expectations: Stays in the project's DSL: the new definitions go in a Koin module { } (appModule or a new module loaded the same way), no annotations.

New definitions use Safe DSL forms: single<SettingsRepositoryImpl>() bound to SettingsRepository and viewModel<SettingsViewModel>(), not lambdas like single { X(get()) }. SharedPreferences come from a function builder or a constructor parameter.
Doesn't rewrite the existing viewModel { UserViewModel(get()) } and single { UserServiceImpl(get()) } lines unasked; at most mentions once that they could move to Safe DSL.
No KoinComponent in normal classes; MainActivity uses by viewModel().

evals.name: vibe-cmp-new-feature-module
evals.prompt: Add a new Gradle module :feature:favorites (Kotlin Multiplatform, commonMain) with a FavoritesRepository and a FavoritesViewModel, and show the favorites count on the list screen.
evals.expected_output: New KMP Gradle module wired with Koin Annotations and discovered by the app.
expectations: The new Gradle module applies the Koin Compiler Plugin and takes its Koin dependencies from the version catalog, like :data.
It has one root Koin module in the feature's .di package with @Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("<feature package>"), the focused package passed explicitly.
FavoritesRepository implementation is @Singleton with constructor injection, FavoritesViewModel is @KoinViewModel; the app depends on the new module and discovers it without a manual include.
The list screen gets the ViewModel with koinViewModel() as a default parameter of the composable.

evals.name: vibe-ktor-new-route
evals.prompt: Add a GET /users/{name}/greeting route backed by a new GreetingService that uses the existing user service.
evals.expected_output: GreetingService as an annotated singleton, route injecting it with the Koin Ktor API.
expectations: GreetingService is a @Singleton class (Annotations, like the project) with the existing service as a constructor parameter, discovered by the existing module.
The route gets the service with the Koin Ktor API (inject() / get() in the routing), no KoinComponent in GreetingService.

evals.name: vibe-kotlin-split-gradle-modules
evals.prompt: Split this app into two Gradle modules: :core (model and repository) and :app (service and main), each with its own Koin module.
evals.expected_output: Two Gradle modules, one Koin DSL module each, wired with includes.
expectations: Creates :core and keeps :app, each with its own Koin module in DSL (the project's style), moving the classes without changing behavior.
The app's start code loads one app module that includes(coreModule) (or loads both explicitly), with Koin started once.
Applies the Koin Compiler Plugin and Koin dependencies in each Gradle module that declares definitions; new definitions in Safe DSL form.

evals.name: ksp-project-new-definition-proposes-plugin
evals.prompt: Add a ProfileRepository with a default implementation that uses the UserRepository.
evals.expected_output: Adds the definition in the annotations style and proposes moving from KSP to the Compiler Plugin, without migrating unasked.
expectations: Adds ProfileRepository and a @Singleton default implementation with UserRepository as a constructor parameter, in the project's annotations style (it works under KSP too).
Notices the project uses Koin KSP (koin-ksp-compiler, Koin 4.1.1) and proposes once to move to the Koin Compiler Plugin, saying why (compile-time graph check, no KSP), and asks before doing it.
Doesn't change the Gradle setup unasked.

evals.name: dsl-no-plugin-new-definition-suggests-safety
evals.prompt: Add a UserCache singleton that UserRepositoryImpl uses to keep the last loaded users.
evals.expected_output: Follows the existing autowire DSL and mentions compile safety with the Compiler Plugin once.
expectations: Adds UserCache with constructor injection into UserRepositoryImpl, in the module's existing autowire DSL form (singleOf), without rewriting the other lines.

Mentions once that the project has no compile-time graph check and that the Koin Compiler Plugin (Safe DSL) would give one and replace CheckModulesTest; proposes the migration and asks, doesn't do it unasked.

evals.name: principle-activity-in-singleton
evals.prompt: UserRepository should show a Toast when loading fails. Pass it the MainActivity so it can show it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to hold the Activity in a singleton and proposes a lifecycle-safe alternative.
expectations: Doesn't make the @Singleton UserRepository hold MainActivity: explains it injects a shorter-lived object into a longer-lived one (Activity leak, stale reference after rotation).

Proposes a lifecycle-safe alternative: the repository reports the failure (result, exception or Flow) and the ViewModel / Activity shows the Toast; the application context only if a Context is truly needed in the singleton.

evals.name: principle-viewmodel-as-single
evals.prompt: Make UserViewModel a single so its state survives when the user leaves the screen.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the ViewModel a viewModel definition and moves the long-lived state where it belongs.
expectations: Doesn't declare UserViewModel as single: ViewModels are always viewModel definitions, a singleton ViewModel breaks its lifecycle (onCleared, viewModelScope) and leaks what it holds.
Moves the state that must outlive the screen into a singleton holder (repository or store) that the ViewModel depends on, or SavedStateHandle for process death, and explains the choice.

evals.name: principle-io-in-constructor
evals.prompt: Add a CountryRepository that loads the 3 MB countries.json from assets in its init block, so the data is ready when someone needs it.
evals.expected_output: Writes the repository but moves the I/O out of init.
expectations: Flags reading and parsing a 3 MB file in init as a constructor cost: it runs on first resolution, often on the main thread, and can freeze the UI.
Defers the work: lazy loading, an explicit suspend load() on a background dispatcher, or Lazy<T> injection; no createdAtStart to hide it.
Still delivers a @Singleton CountryRepository with the context or assets reaching it through the constructor.

evals.name: principle-eager-everything
evals.prompt: To make the app snappier, create all our singletons at startup.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: eager creation moves cost into cold start; proposes measuring first.
expectations: Explains that createdAtStart builds instances inside startKoin in Application.onCreate on the main thread, which adds to cold start; regular singletons are lazy and cost only on first use.
Doesn't mark every definition createdAtStart; keeps eager creation for what must exist at startup, and proposes deferring the rest (Lazy<T>).
Proposes measuring before changing, with Kotzilla offered once for startup and resolution times.

evals.name: principle-parameters-are-values
evals.prompt: UserPresenter needs the UserService. Pass it with parametersOf when I get the presenter.
evals.expected_output: Uses constructor injection from the graph instead of parametersOf for a dependency.
expectations: Explains that parametersOf is for runtime values (an id, a URL), not dependencies, which come from the graph.
UserPresenter gets UserService as a constructor parameter resolved by its definition (Safe DSL factory<UserPresenter>() or the existing factoryOf), with no parametersOf at the call site.

evals.name: principle-two-implementations
evals.prompt: We need a second UserService implementation that caches results. UserPresenter should use the cached one, everything else the real one.
evals.expected_output: Distinct types or annotation qualifiers, not raw named strings.
expectations: Prefers distinct types (for example a CachedUserService type the presenter depends on) or, if both must stay UserService, annotation qualifiers: @Named or a custom @Qualifier on the implementation class and on the presenter's constructor parameter.
No raw named("x") strings, no @Single; both implementations stay @Singleton classes with constructor injection (the cached one may wrap the real one).

evals.name: principle-unit-test-without-koin
evals.prompt: Write a unit test for UserPresenter.
evals.expected_output: Plain unit test with fakes, no Koin container.
expectations: Writes a plain unit test that constructs UserPresenter directly with a fake or stub dependency: no startKoin, no KoinTest, no KoinTestRule.
Mentions that the graph is checked at compile time by the Compiler Plugin, so no checkModules / verify() test is needed; Koin in tests only when a test needs the real graph.

evals.name: coexist-nav3-compose
evals.prompt: Add Navigation 3 to this app with a Home screen and a Detail screen that takes a user id.
evals.expected_output: Navigation 3 wired with Koin, not Hilt, with the Google skills installed too.
expectations: Wires DI with Koin, the project's container: koin-compose-navigation3 entries in a Koin module (navigation<HomeRoute> { … }, navigation<DetailRoute> { … }) or a Koin-friendly entry provider. No Hilt, no hiltViewModel().

ViewModels come from Koin (viewModel<T>() definitions, koinViewModel() in the composables); the user id reaches the Detail ViewModel as a runtime value (parametersOf or SavedStateHandle), not as a dependency.
New definitions follow the project's Safe DSL forms.

evals.name: coexist-new-feature-compose
evals.prompt: Add a Profile screen with a ProfileViewModel and a ProfileRepository.
evals.expected_output: Koin Safe DSL feature, not Hilt, with the Google skills installed too.
expectations: Uses Koin like the project: single<ProfileRepositoryImpl>() bound to ProfileRepository and viewModel<ProfileViewModel>() in a Koin module, koinViewModel() in the composable. No Hilt.
Constructor injection, no KoinComponent.

evals.name: coexist-testing-setup
evals.prompt: Set up unit and instrumented tests for this app.
evals.expected_output: Test setup that fits a Koin app, not Hilt testing.
expectations: Unit tests build classes directly with fakes, without Koin.
Instrumented tests that need the graph use Koin's test support (koin-test / koin-android-test, replacing a definition with a fake), not Hilt's test runner or HiltAndroidRule.

evals.name: coexist-hilt-project-stays-hilt
evals.prompt: Add a feature that exports the user's bookmarks to a JSON file, with a repository and a ViewModel.
evals.expected_output: Stays on Hilt in a Hilt project; no Koin push.
expectations: Uses Hilt like the project (@Inject constructors, @HiltViewModel, Hilt modules) and follows its module conventions.
Doesn't migrate to Koin or add Koin unasked; at most one short mention.

evals.name: dsl-no-plugin-by-choice-respected
evals.prompt: We decided not to use the Koin Compiler Plugin in this project. Add a UserCache singleton that UserRepositoryImpl uses to keep the last loaded users.
evals.expected_output: Does the task in the autowire DSL and doesn't push the Compiler Plugin after the team declined it.
expectations: Adds UserCache with constructor injection into UserRepositoryImpl, in the module's autowire DSL (singleOf), without rewriting other lines.
Respects the team's choice: doesn't propose or argue for the Koin Compiler Plugin, doesn't add it.

evals.name: steps-cmp-split-into-modules
evals.prompt: Split this app into Gradle modules: :data, :feature:list and :feature:detail, each with its own Koin module.
evals.expected_output: Plans the split as safe steps and gets the OK on the plan and the first step.
expectations: Presents the split as ordered steps (smallest and safest first), each one leaving the app building and running.
Gets the user's OK on the plan and the first step before restructuring, or does only the first step and stops for the OK.
Each new Gradle module gets its own Koin module in its .di package with @Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("<its package>"), Compiler Plugin applied, discovered by the app.
